# Wedding Photo and Video Brief Builder for Post-Production Teams

*Generated by Forge on 2026-05-29T12:18:09.850Z — score 8.6/10*

## Overview

**SaaS web app:** Build a responsive Next.js SaaS called **BriefedWed** that helps wedding photographers, videographers, and hybrid studios generate structured post-production briefs for outsourced editors, internal assistants, and social-content contractors. The product solves the recurring handoff problem after each wedding: turning scattered notes, couple preferences, vendor details, music direction, culling instructions, cue points, and social deliverable requirements into repeatable, exportable briefs for full films, highlight films, sneak peeks, Lightroom/photo edits, Instagram Reels, TikToks, and vendor promo clips.

## Why this will succeed

### Comparable products that are working

1. **Aftershoot** — https://aftershoot.com  
   Aftershoot is an established AI culling and editing SaaS for professional photographers. The research identifies it as a known paid subscription product in the professional photography workflow category. What works: photographers already pay for software that saves time in post-production, especially around culling and editing.

2. **Imagen** — https://imagen-ai.com  
   Imagen is an established AI photo editing platform used by professional photographers, with per-photo and subscription-style pricing depending on plan/version. What works: it proves that photographers will pay for automation and repeatable editing workflows when the product saves time across many shoots.

3. **Studio Ninja** — https://www.studioninja.co  
   Studio Ninja is an established CRM/workflow SaaS for photographers with paid monthly plans in the professional photography software category. What works: wedding and portrait photographers already buy niche workflow tools for client management, invoicing, contracts, and business operations.

Additional proof of paid demand in this vertical: **ShootDotEdit** — https://shootdotedit.com — is a long-running outsourced photo editing service for wedding photographers, showing that photographers already pay to delegate editing work.

### Why this specific opportunity is different / better

The opportunity is not to compete with Aftershoot, Imagen, Studio Ninja, or ShootDotEdit directly.

The gap is the **communication and handoff layer**:

- **Aftershoot** focuses on AI culling and editing, not on generating human-readable outsourced editor briefs, social cut instructions, vendor deliverables, cue-point notes, or wedding-specific post-production packages.
- **Imagen** optimizes photo editing and personal AI profiles, but does not help videographers create teaser briefs, Instagram Reel instructions, TikTok cut notes, ceremony/reception pacing guidance, or music-direction documents.
- **Studio Ninja** is strong for CRM, quotes, invoices, contracts, and workflow automation, but not post-production creative handoff.
- **ShootDotEdit** is a done-for-you editing vendor, not a neutral reusable brief builder that works with any editor, VA, contractor, or internal assistant.

BriefedWed wins by being a **wedding-specific post-production brief system**, not a generic AI prompt wrapper and not a full editing platform. The product’s job is to reduce miscommunication, avoid revision rounds, and make each wedding’s deliverables easier to hand off.

## Target user

Primary persona: **solo or small-team wedding videographer who delivers highlight films plus social clips and occasionally outsources editing.**

They shoot weddings on weekends, then manage a backlog of footage, notes, speeches, vows, music preferences, vendor credits, and social deliverables. They may use an external editor, a VA, a second shooter, or an internal assistant for first cuts, Reels, TikToks, sneak peeks, or full wedding films.

Current workflow:

- Notes in Apple Notes, Google Docs, Notion, email threads, texts, or memory
- Vendor tags copied from Instagram
- Couple preferences buried in questionnaires
- Editor instructions written from scratch for every wedding
- Separate ad hoc notes for full film, teaser, Reel, TikTok, and vendor promo clips
- Revisions caused by missing context, unclear pacing, or forgotten must-have moments

Why current options fail:

- Generic docs/templates are not structured around wedding deliverables.
- AI video tools focus on cutting content, not on communicating creative intent.
- Photography CRMs manage clients and invoices, not post-production handoffs.
- Outsourced editing services solve editing labor, not repeatable brief creation across multiple vendors.

Where they hang out online:

- r/WeddingVideography
- r/WeddingPhotography
- r/videography
- Photography business Facebook groups
- YouTube channels and educators focused on wedding photography/videography workflows
- Communities and comment sections around outsourced wedding editing, culling, Lightroom presets, and social delivery workflows

Secondary persona: **wedding photographer who outsources culling or Lightroom editing** and needs a repeatable culling/editing brief for each gallery.

## Core features (MVP)

- **User authentication**
  - Google OAuth login.
  - Email/account page.
  - Free trial state or unpaid account state.

- **Project dashboard**
  - List of wedding projects.
  - Create new wedding project.
  - Duplicate previous wedding project.
  - Filter by draft/completed/exported.

- **Wedding project setup**
  - Couple names.
  - Wedding date.
  - Venue name/location.
  - Photographer/videographer brand name.
  - Internal project notes.
  - Editor name/email optional.

- **Vendor directory per project**
  - Add vendors:
    - Planner
    - Venue
    - Photographer
    - Videographer
    - Florist
    - DJ/band
    - Hair/makeup
    - Dress
    - Other
  - Fields:
    - Vendor name
    - Instagram handle
    - Website
    - Notes
  - Reuse vendors across projects.

- **Deliverable selector**
  - Full wedding film
  - Highlight film
  - Ceremony edit
  - Speeches edit
  - Sneak peek
  - Instagram Reel
  - TikTok
  - Vendor promo clip
  - Photo culling brief
  - Lightroom/photo editing brief

- **Brief builder forms**
  - Structured form fields based on deliverable type.
  - Must-have moments.
  - Avoid moments.
  - Music direction.
  - Pacing/emotional tone.
  - Color/style notes.
  - Audio priorities.
  - Orientation/aspect ratio.
  - Target length.
  - Caption/on-screen text notes.
  - Vendor tag requirements.
  - Deadline.
  - Reference links.

- **Saved style guides**
  - Brand/studio style guide:
    - Editing style
    - Color preferences
    - Music preferences
    - Common intro/outro notes
    - Social caption style
    - Delivery defaults
  - Apply style guide to a new brief.

- **AI-assisted brief generation**
  - Generate a polished brief from structured fields.
  - No video upload or video analysis in MVP.
  - User can edit generated text before export.
  - Use explicit templates and optional AI polish rather than pretending to inspect footage.

- **Export options**
  - Export as clean web page/share link.
  - Copy to clipboard.
  - Download as PDF using browser print or server-side PDF generation if simple.
  - Markdown export.
  - Plain text export.

- **Free template generator**
  - Public unauthenticated pages allow users to generate one simple brief.
  - Require signup to save, duplicate, export multiple briefs, or use style guides.

- **Stripe subscription gating**
  - Free: 1 saved project, 1 export, public template generator.
  - Paid: unlimited projects, saved style guides, reusable vendors, exports, duplicate projects.

- **Basic onboarding**
  - Ask user:
    - Photographer, videographer, or hybrid studio?
    - Do they outsource editing?
    - Main deliverables?
  - Preload relevant brief templates.

## Tech stack recommendation

Use the standard web SaaS stack:

- **Next.js 15 App Router + TypeScript**
- **PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM**
- **Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui components**
- **NextAuth v5 with Google OAuth**
- **Stripe subscriptions**
- **Resend** for transactional emails:
  - Welcome email
  - Export/share email optional
  - Subscription/payment notifications optional
- **OpenAI API or compatible LLM provider** for AI-assisted brief generation
- **Deployed to Coolify using Docker**

This product is a responsive web SaaS. It does not need a native mobile app. Many users may fill in briefs from laptops after a wedding or while reviewing footage, but the app should still be responsive enough for mobile-web use.

## Monetization & pricing

Primary strategy: **subscription SaaS with a limited free template generator.**

Pricing should reflect the value of avoiding revision rounds and saving time across paid wedding jobs. Comparable professional photography workflow/editing products in the research — Aftershoot, Imagen, Studio Ninja, ShootDotEdit — show that photographers pay for workflow and editing infrastructure in the professional SaaS category. The research specifically supports a **$39–79/mo** range.

### Tiers

#### Free

Price: **$0**

Includes:

- Public template generator
- 1 saved wedding project
- 1 export
- Basic brief types:
  - Wedding film editor brief
  - Instagram Reel brief
  - Culling notes brief

Purpose: drive SEO conversion and let users experience the output before paying.

#### Solo

Price: **$39/mo** or **$390/year**

For solo wedding photographers/videographers.

Includes:

- Unlimited wedding projects
- Unlimited brief generation
- Unlimited exports

#### Studio

Price: **$79/mo** or **$790/year**

For small teams, hybrid studios, and users working with multiple editors.

Includes everything in Solo, plus:

#### One-off pack

Price: **$15 one-time**

Includes:

Purpose: capture users who do not want a subscription yet and later upsell them after the next wedding.

## Revenue model

- Conservative case from research: roughly **100 subscribers at $39/mo** plus occasional one-offs, or around **$4,000 MRR**.
- Optimistic case from research: **400–500 subscribers** at roughly **$60 ARPA**, or up to approximately **$30,000 MRR**.

### Funnel assumptions

Early funnel:

- SEO/community visitors land on template pages.
- Visitors generate a free brief.
- Some create accounts to save/export.
- Some subscribe when they need repeat use or multiple exports.

  - 5% one-off packs

### Month 3

### Month 6

- Key features:
  - Done-for-you wedding photo editing
  - Editing delegation for photographers
- Gaps/weaknesses:
  - It is a service vendor, not a neutral brief builder.
  - Does not address videography/social cut briefs.
  - Does not provide a lightweight reusable SaaS workflow for teams using multiple editors or contractors.
- Differentiation:
  - BriefedWed works with any editor, internal assistant, freelancer, or post-production partner.

## Timeline

### Week 1 — Core data model and app shell

Build:

- Initialize Next.js app.
- Set up PostgreSQL and Prisma.
- Add NextAuth Google OAuth.
- Create main app layout and marketing layout.
- Build dashboard shell.
- Implement data models:
  - User
  - Account
  - Session
  - WeddingProject
  - Vendor
  - ProjectVendor
  - StyleGuide
  - Brief
  - Subscription
- Build project creation flow:
  - Couple names
  - Date
  - Venue
  - Brand/studio name
  - Notes
- Build project list dashboard.

### Week 2 — Brief builder MVP

Build:

- Deliverable selector.
- Dynamic brief form based on deliverable type.
- Brief field components:
  - Text input
  - Textarea
  - Select
  - Multi-select/checklist
  - Date/deadline
  - Reference link list
- Add brief templates for:
  - Wedding film editor brief
  - Instagram Reel/TikTok brief

- Implement save/edit brief.
- Implement deterministic template-based brief output.

### Week 3 — Exports, style guides, payments

Build:

- Apply style guide to brief.

- Export:

### Week 4 — SEO templates, onboarding, polish

Build:

### Week 5 — Launch

Build-only tasks:

- Deploy production app to Coolify.

## Score breakdown

- **recurringRevenue: 8/10** — Wedding post-production is recurring across every wedding season, and saved templates/style guides make subscription retention plausible.
- **buildComplexity: 7/10** — MVP is manageable for a solo developer because it is mostly forms, templates, exports, auth, and payments; complexity increases only if video upload/analysis is added, which is excluded from MVP.
- **marketValidation: 8/10** — Comparable products like Aftershoot, Imagen, Studio Ninja, and ShootDotEdit show photographers pay for workflow, editing, and outsourcing infrastructure.
- **competition: 7/10** — There are strong adjacent products, but the specific brief-generation/handoff layer for wedding post-production is under-addressed.
- **automationPotential: 8/10** — Structured inputs plus AI-assisted writing can turn repetitive notes into polished briefs without needing full video analysis.
- **platformFit: 9/10** — A responsive web SaaS is ideal for project dashboards, templates, exports, billing, and editor share links.
- **distributionFeasibility: 8/10** — Driven by long-tail SEO around wedding editing briefs, outsourcing workflows, culling notes, and social cut templates, plus community seeding in wedding photography/videography groups.

## Build instructions for the coding agent

1. Initialize the app:

   `npx create-next-app@latest wedding-photo-video-brief-builder-post-production --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*"`

2. Install required dependencies:

   `npm install prisma @prisma/client next-auth @auth/prisma-adapter stripe resend zod react-hook-form @hookform/resolvers nanoid date-fns openai`

3. Install shadcn/ui:

   `npx shadcn@latest init`

   Add components:

   `npx shadcn@latest add button card input textarea select checkbox badge dialog dropdown-menu form table tabs toast separator sheet`

4. Set up Prisma:

   `npx prisma init`

   Configure `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`.

5. Define Prisma schema in `prisma/schema.prisma` with these models:

   - `User`
   - `Account`
   - `Session`
   - `VerificationToken`
   - `WeddingProject`
   - `Vendor`
   - `ProjectVendor`
   - `StyleGuide`
   - `Brief`
   - `Subscription`

6. Use these core data shapes:

   `WeddingProject`:
   - `id`
   - `userId`
   - `coupleNames`
   - `weddingDate`
   - `venueName`
   - `venueLocation`
   - `brandName`
   - `notes`
   - `status`
   - `createdAt`
   - `updatedAt`

   `Brief`:
   - `id`
   - `projectId`
   - `userId`
   - `type`
   - `title`
   - `formData Json`
   - `generatedText`
   - `status`
   - `shareToken`
   - `createdAt`
   - `updatedAt`

   `StyleGuide`:
   - `id`
   - `userId`
   - `name`
   - `editingStyle`
   - `colorPreferences`
   - `musicPreferences`
   - `pacingNotes`
   - `socialCaptionStyle`
   - `deliveryDefaults Json`
   - `createdAt`
   - `updatedAt`

   `Vendor`:
   - `id`
   - `userId`
   - `name`
   - `category`
   - `instagramHandle`
   - `website`
   - `notes`

   `Subscription`:
   - `id`
   - `userId`
   - `stripeCustomerId`
   - `stripeSubscriptionId`
   - `status`
   - `priceId`
   - `plan`
   - `currentPeriodEnd`

7. Run:

   `npx prisma generate`

   Then create initial migration:

   `npx prisma migrate dev --name init`

8. Configure NextAuth v5 with Google OAuth and Prisma adapter.

   Create:

   - `src/auth.ts`
   - `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`

   Environment variables:

   - `AUTH_SECRET`
   - `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`
   - `AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET`

9. Create app route groups:

   - `src/app/(marketing)/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(marketing)/templates/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(marketing)/templates/[slug]/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/projects/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/projects/new/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/projects/[projectId]/briefs/new/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/projects/[projectId]/briefs/[briefId]/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/style-guides/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/(app)/vendors/page.tsx`
   - `src/app/share/[shareToken]/page.tsx`

10. Create reusable UI components:

   - `src/components/marketing/Header.tsx`
   - `src/components/marketing/Footer.tsx`
   - `src/components/marketing/TemplateCta.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/AppSidebar.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/ProjectCard.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/BriefTypeSelector.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/BriefForm.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/BriefPreview.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/ExportMenu.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/UpgradeDialog.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/StyleGuideForm.tsx`
   - `src/components/app/VendorForm.tsx`

11. Create brief template definitions in:

   `src/lib/brief-templates.ts`

   Include these brief types:

   - `WEDDING_FILM`
   - `HIGHLIGHT_FILM`
   - `SOCIAL_REEL`
   - `TIKTOK`
   - `SNEAK_PEEK`
   - `VENDOR_PROMO`
   - `PHOTO_CULLING`
   - `LIGHTROOM_EDITING`

   Each template should define:
   - `label`
   - `description`
   - `fields`
   - `defaultOutputSections`

12. Implement deterministic brief generation in:

   `src/lib/generate-brief.ts`

   Function:

   `generateBriefText({ project, vendors, styleGuide, briefType, formData }): string`

   Output sections should include:

   - Project overview
   - Couple and wedding details
   - Deliverable requirements
   - Must-have moments
   - Avoid / do-not-use notes
   - Style and pacing
   - Music/audio direction
   - Vendor credits/tags
   - Technical specs
   - Deadline and delivery notes

13. Add optional AI polish endpoint:

   `src/app/api/briefs/polish/route.ts`

   Behavior:

   - Accept generated deterministic text.
   - Ask LLM to improve clarity and formatting only.
   - Do not claim to analyze footage.
   - Return editable text.
   - If no API key is present, gracefully return deterministic text.

14. Implement project CRUD server actions in:

   - `src/app/(app)/projects/actions.ts`
   - `src/app/(app)/vendors/actions.ts`
   - `src/app/(app)/style-guides/actions.ts`
   - `src/app/(app)/projects/[projectId]/briefs/actions.ts`

   Validate all inputs with Zod.

15. Implement subscription gating in:

   `src/lib/permissions.ts`

   Rules:

   - Free users can create 1 project.
   - Free users can export 1 brief.
   - Free users cannot create saved style guides beyond one default.
   - Paid users have unlimited projects/briefs/exports.
   - Studio users can create multiple style guides and editor presets.

16. Set up Stripe.

   Create:

   - `src/lib/stripe.ts`
   - `src/app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts`
   - `src/app/api/stripe/portal/route.ts`
   - `src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts`

   Stripe products:

   - Solo monthly: $39/mo
   - Solo yearly: $390/year
   - Studio monthly: $79/mo
   - Studio yearly: $790/year
   - One-off brief pack: $15

17. Add Resend email integration.

   Create:

   - `src/lib/resend.ts`
   - `src/emails/WelcomeEmail.tsx`

   Send welcome email after first account creation if practical. If event hook is too complex for MVP, add email utility but defer sending until after launch.

18. Build public SEO template pages from a static config:

   `src/lib/seo-templates.ts`

   Include the 10 priority template pages listed in the PRD. Each page should render:

   - H1
   - Intro
   - When to use this template
   - What to include
   - Example brief excerpt
   - Embedded free generator CTA
   - FAQ section
   - Signup CTA

19. Build free unauthenticated generator:

   - Route: `src/app/(marketing)/free-brief-generator/page.tsx`
   - Let user choose one brief type and fill simplified fields.
   - Generate preview without account.
   - Require signup to save/export.

20. Add export functionality.

   In `ExportMenu.tsx`, include:

   - Copy to clipboard
   - Download Markdown
   - Print/save as PDF using print stylesheet
   - Share link generation

   Create share link by setting `Brief.shareToken` with `nanoid()`.

21. Add analytics event hooks.

   Create:

   `src/lib/analytics.ts`

   Track:

   - `template_page_view`
   - `free_brief_generated`
   - `signup_started`
   - `project_created`
   - `brief_created`
   - `brief_exported`
   - `checkout_started`
   - `subscription_created`

   Keep implementation provider-agnostic so Plausible/PostHog can be added via env vars.

22. Add sitemap and robots.

   Create:

   - `src/app/sitemap.ts`
   - `src/app/robots.ts`

   Include all marketing/template pages.

23. Add production metadata.

   In `src/app/layout.tsx`, configure default title:

   `BriefedWed — Wedding Editor Brief Generator`

   Default description:

   `Create wedding photo and video editing briefs for outsourced editors, Reels, TikToks, sneak peeks, culling, Lightroom edits, and vendor deliverables.`

24. Add responsive polish.

   Ensure all dashboard and builder pages work at:
   - 390px mobile width
   - 768px tablet width
   - 1280px desktop width

   Use shadcn cards, tabs, dialogs, and forms.

25. Verify build:

   `npm run lint`

   `npm run build`

26. Configure Next.js standalone output.

   In `next.config.ts`, set:

   `output: "standalone"`

27. Create Dockerfile for Coolify deployment.

   Use a multi-stage Node build that:
   - Installs dependencies
   - Runs Prisma generate
   - Builds Next.js
   - Copies standalone output
   - Starts server with `node server.js`

28. Add deployment environment variables in Coolify:

   - `DATABASE_URL`
   - `AUTH_SECRET`
   - `AUTH_URL`
   - `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`
   - `AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET`
   - `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`
   - `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`
   - `RESEND_API_KEY`
   - `OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`

29. Run production migration:

   `npx prisma migrate deploy`

30. Final launch checklist:

   - Confirm Google login works.
   - Confirm project creation works.
   - Confirm brief generation works.
   - Confirm share links work.
   - Confirm exports work.
   - Confirm Stripe checkout and webhook update subscription status.
   - Confirm free user limits work.
   - Confirm sitemap loads.
   - Confirm `npm run build` passes.
   - Deploy to Coolify.
